thread.title: 3 Hot Warren Buffett Stocks To Buy Now

author: TipRanks
title: 3 Hot Warren Buffett Stocks To Buy Now
text:
Shutterstock photo In 1996, Warren Buffett wrote to shareholders in Berkshire Hathaway, “If you aren't willing to own a stock for ten years, don't even think about owning it for ten minutes.” His farsighted mindset has informed his whole investment career, and his habit of making very long-term investments frequently leads him away from the profit churning, high yield stocks that typically get the hype.
In recent days, however, several of Buffett’s big-name investment choices have been attracting positive reviews from some of Wall Street’s top-rated analysts. Let’s unpack the TipRanks data , and see why the analysts are coming around to Buffett’s choices.
Apple, Inc.
Warren Buffett’s single largest stock holding is one of his very few investments in the tech industry. He started buying Apple ( AAPL – Research Report ) back in 2016, when it was trading in the low $100s. AAPL is at $154 today, even after its long decline through the last quarter of 2018, so Buffett is still far ahead on this investment. He currently holds over 250 million shares in the company, valued at almost $40 billion.
Apple’s current share price is 33% down from its October peak of $232. The long, steep slide seems to have ended, however, as the stock has been mostly flat since Christmas. There was a brief slip at the start of the year when CEO Tim Cook talked down the Q1 forward guidance, but that may have turned out to be a blip. Apple has received several ‘buy’ ratings by top-rated analysts over the last few days.
On Jan 18, Amit Daryanani ( Track Record & Ratings ) or RBC Capital, set a $185 price target – suggesting a 20% upside to the stock – and noted that Apple is restructuring its revenue reporting to reflect the increased importance of the Services Division while hardware sales are declining. He noted that Maps, Siri, and iCloud have all been moved from product sales to services and will boost the services earnings by more than $2.5 billion. He also notes that Apple’s R&D spending continues to grow.
More recently, five-star Monness analyst Brian White ( Track Record & Ratings ) ranked #35 overall in the TipRanks database and #25 among tech-sector analysts, acknowledges Apple’s near-term weakness, but sees great potential for long-term strength: “We believe Apple will benefit in the long run from its shift to a higher percentage of sales from Services, low market share across key product categories, the rise of the global middle class, opportunities for new product areas that leverage Apple’s vast digital ecosystem...” White gives Apple a 30% upside and a $200 price target.
Finally, on Jan 23, D.A. Davidson’s Tom Forte ( Track Record & Ratings ) set a price target of $245, Apple’s highest price target in months. Like White, Forte admits that iPhone sales are likely to remain soft, but notes several short-term boosters for AAPL, including: “…better-than-expected results from its newer products Apple Watch and HomePod as well as an accelerated repurchase effort and increase in dividends.” Forte’s price target implies a 59% upside to AAPL, indicating that the company has plenty of latent strength.
Overall, AAPL holds a ‘Moderate Buy’ on the analyst consensus, based on an even split between ‘buy’ and ‘hold’ ratings: 18 of each. The current share price is $154, so the average price target of $184 gives it a 20% upside potential.
General Motors Company
Buffett has a $2 billion stake in GM ( GM – Research Report ), totaling 52 million shares. His large investment in an old-time industrial giant has raised eyebrows; over the last year, auto industry analysts have noted that GM has lower cash holdings than its competitors and falling sales numbers. So, what did Buffett see that the rest of us did not? And why are the analysts starting to turn around on their assessments?
For starters, GM does have some “invisible assets.” The company has a widespread infrastructure of manufacturing plants, including 12 assembly factories and 12 powertrain factories plus component warehouses, tooling facilities, and a battery assembly plant. And that’s just in the US. GM has plants in China, Mexico, and Canada, too. While the plants are subject to seasonal layoffs or downtimes, simply having so much latent manufacturing capability puts GM in a strong position to take advantage of a market upturn.
In addition, this puts GM in a fine position to take advantage of fleet sales. There is a reason why so many car rental agencies offer Chevy models – GM has made the low-cost, generic fleet vehicle, like the Impala, into a successful niche.
So, GM, while it has its struggles, it also has ways out. Citigroup’s analyst Itay Michaeli ( Track Record & Ratings ) recently took note of that, writing that GM can use its successful pickup trucks to boost the share price: “Strong guidance and truck remessaging highlight that Pickups have undergone many years of significant demand expansion that will be sustainable for years to come… GM should take the next step forward and re-segment Pickups outside of traditional auto segments.” Michaeli gives GM a $60 target price, suggesting a 59% upside to the stock. His rating is one of 6 ‘buy’ ratings in a row that this stock has received.
Also among the recent spate of strong ratings was five-star analyst Ryan Brinkman ( Track Record & Ratings ) of J.P. Morgan. Brinkman sees GM benefitting from “revenue tailwinds from a richer mix of Cadillacs and crossovers, and cost tailwinds from efficiency initiatives,” and sets a $53 price target on the stock, giving a 40% upside from the current share price of $37.
General Motors’ analyst consensus rating is a ‘Moderate Buy,’ based on 8 ‘buy’ ratings – including those 6 in a row in the last three weeks! – and 3 ‘holds.’ The stock’s average price target is $46, which suggests a 20% upside.
Visa, Inc.
At 10 million shares and $1.4 billion, this is the smallest of the ‘Buffett holdings’ we are looking at today. But it’s also one of the best performing. Visa is up 11% over the last 12 months, a good performance for any investment. Along with stakes in Mastercard and Amex, Buffett’s Visa holding is part of his interest in payment processors.
With a worldwide network of 3 billion cards in circulation, and more than 44 million merchants who will accept them, Visa is in a fine place to take advantage of its basic business mode: fees on every transaction. More importantly than that, as a credit card company, Visa is perfectly positioned to profit from the world’s accelerating transition away from cash transactions.
That explains why, in the last month, Visa ( V – Research Report ) has received 3 ‘buy’ ratings in a row, including from the #5 financial analyst in the TipRanks database, David Koning ( Track Record & Ratings ) of Baird. Koning looks at Visa’s recent acquisition activity, and says, “[The] risk/reward on Visa remains favorable following its acquisition of London-listed Earthport. The company is a cross-border provider for banks and businesses and could add roughly 0.2% to Visa's annual revenue…” He gives the company a $150 price target, for a 10% upside.
Visa also received a ‘buy’ rating from Piper Jaffray’s Jason Deleeuw ( Track Record & Ratings ). Deleeuw takes a more aggressive stance on the stock, with a $178 target and 30% upside, saying that he “continues to see Visa as a multi-vector long-term growth story with contained risks.”
The analysts agree that Visa is a ‘buy,’ and Visa holds a ‘Strong Buy’ in the analyst consensus. Shares trade for $137, so the $164 average price target gives a 19% upside.
Author: Michael Marcus
